players.product: boiler + steam-turbine power plants (coal / natural gas, enhanced combined cycle) for AI data-center campuses (Base Electron project, North Dakota)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K): bookings were $151.0 million in Q2 2026, a 38% increase over Q2 2025; Q2 revenue was primarily driven by an increase in large project volume, including $100.7 million from Base Electron. The investor presentation gives revenue of ~$834.3M and adjusted EBITDA of $63.8 million for the trailing twelve months ended June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 bookings $151.0 million (+38%); Q2 Base Electron revenue $100.7 million; TTM revenue ~$834.3M

quarterly_data.signal: Investor presentation (August 2026): the $2.4B, 1.2 GW power project for Base Electron will be located near Center, North Dakota, and its Conditional Use Permit was submitted in August 2026; B&W provides four 300 MW natural-gas boilers, and the deck cites future expansion potential for another 1.2 GW. B&W also lists a strategic partnership with Denham Capital to convert existing coal plants to power data centers in the U.S. and Europe, and offers off-the-shelf 50 and 300 MW natural gas-fired boiler and steam turbine designs for AI factories and data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.2 GW Base Electron project ($2.4B); future expansion potential another 1.2 GW

contracts.signal: B&W's August 2026 investor presentation (8-K Exhibit 99.2): Siemens Energy is supplying the steam turbine generator sets for the $2.4B, 1.2 GW Base Electron project, paired with four B&W 300 MW natural-gas boilers; B&W says the combination enables years-faster deployment than traditional combined- or simple-cycle gas turbine projects. CEO Kenneth Young (release): B&W's natural gas-fired boilers are being provided alongside Siemens Energy steam turbine systems.
